sn9.14:0.2: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.14:1.1: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.14:1.2: Now on that occasion, when he had returned from his alms round, after his meal that bhikkhu used to descend into a pond and sniff a red lotus.
sn9.14:1.3: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, having compassion for that bhikkhu, desiring his good, desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in him, approached him and addressed him in verse:
sn9.14:2.1: “When you sniff this lotus flower, An item that has not been given,
sn9.14:2.2: This is one factor of theft:
sn9.14:2.3: You, dear sir, are a thief of scent.”
sn9.14:2.4: You, dear sir, are a thief of scent.”
sn9.14:3.1: “I do not take, I do not damage,
sn9.14:3.2: I sniff the lotus from afar;
sn9.14:3.3: So for what reason do you say
sn9.14:3.4: That I am a thief of scent?
sn9.14:4.1: “One who digs up the lotus stalks,
sn9.14:4.4: Why is he not spoken to?”
sn9.14:5.1: “When a person is rough and fierce, Badly soiled like a nursing cloth,
sn9.14:5.2: I have nothing to say to him;
sn9.14:5.3: But it’s to you that I ought to speak.
sn9.14:5.4: But it’s to you that I ought to speak.
sn9.14:6.1: “For a person without blemish, Always in quest of purity,
sn9.14:6.3: Even a mere hair’s tip of evil
sn9.14:6.4: Appears as big as a cloud.”
sn9.14:7.2: And you have compassion for me.
sn9.14:7.3: Please, O spirit, speak to me again,
sn9.14:7.4: Whenever you see such a deed.”
sn9.14:8.2: Nor are we your hired servant.
sn9.14:8.3: You, bhikkhu, should know for yourself
sn9.14:8.4: The way to a good destination.”
sn9.14:9.1: Then that bhikkhu, stirred by that devatā, acquired a sense of urgency.
sn9.14:11.5: The Linked Discourses in the Forest are completed.
